# 0  Purpose and contents

This file complements `rossmann_final_comprehensive.Rmd`. It adds the analyses
recommended for the final thesis version. Each experiment has its own section
and a `RUN_*` switch so expensive parts can be skipped:

| ID | Experiment | Thesis use |
|----|------------|-----------|
| E1 | Fixed-origin **recursive** 42-day forecast with lag features | Separates "information value of lags" from "value of daily updating" (Stage 3b) |
| E2 | **Diebold–Mariano** tests on the primary holdout | Statistical significance of model differences |
| E3 | Stage 2 replication **standard deviations** (number of stores) | Uncertainty bands for subset experiments |
| E4 | **Framework validation**: per-store gain vs.\ predictable variation | Direct test of the Var(delta) mechanism |
| E5 | **Hyperparameter grid** (XGBoost depth x LightGBM leaves) | Is the LightGBM > XGBoost ranking tuning-robust? |
| E6 | **Type-A-only** scale experiment | Separates composition from scale in Prediction 1 |
| E7 | **Global vs.\ local** LightGBM | What does cross-learning contribute? |
| E8 | **Descriptive statistics & EDA exports** | Data section tables/figures, incl. store-type/Sunday table |

```{r run-switches}
RUN_E1_RECURSIVE   <- TRUE
RUN_E2_DM_TESTS    <- TRUE
RUN_E3_SUBSET_SD   <- TRUE   # ~30 boosted fits
RUN_E4_FRAMEWORK   <- TRUE
RUN_E5_GRID        <- TRUE   # 9 boosted fits
RUN_E6_TYPEA_SCALE <- TRUE   # ~30 boosted fits
RUN_E7_GLOBAL_LOCAL<- TRUE   # 1 global + N_LOCAL_STORES small fits
N_LOCAL_STORES     <- 200    # stores sampled for the local-model comparison
```

# 1  Packages, paths, data

Identical preprocessing to the comprehensive file, condensed.

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(xgboost)
library(lightgbm)
library(zoo)
library(forecast)   # dm.test

DATA_DIR   <- "/home/whu/isik.kayra/projects"
TRAIN_CSV  <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "train.csv")
STORE_CSV  <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "store.csv")
OUTPUT_DIR <- "rossmann_outputs"
dir.create(OUTPUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

N_THREADS <- max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L)
SEEDS     <- c(42, 123, 7, 999, 2024)
TEST_DAYS <- 42
```

```{r data-prep}
train_raw <- read_csv(TRAIN_CSV, col_types = cols(
  Store = col_integer(), DayOfWeek = col_integer(),
  Date = col_date(format = "%Y-%m-%d"), Sales = col_double(),
  Customers = col_double(), Open = col_integer(), Promo = col_integer(),
  StateHoliday = col_character(), SchoolHoliday = col_integer()))

store_raw <- read_csv(STORE_CSV, col_types = cols(.default = col_guess(),
  Store = col_integer(), StoreType = col_character()))

# Open-day modelling frame (same feature engineering as the comprehensive file)
df <- train_raw %>%
  filter(Open == 1, Sales > 0) %>%
  left_join(store_raw, by = "Store") %>%
  mutate(
    Year = year(Date), Month = month(Date), Week = isoweek(Date),
    DayOfMonth = mday(Date), Quarter = quarter(Date),
    IsWeekend = as.integer(DayOfWeek %in% c(6, 7)),
    StateHoliday = case_when(StateHoliday == "a" ~ 1L, StateHoliday == "b" ~ 2L,
                             StateHoliday == "c" ~ 3L, TRUE ~ 0L),
    CompetitionOpenMonths = pmax(
      ifelse(!is.na(CompetitionOpenSinceYear) & !is.na(CompetitionOpenSinceMonth),
             (Year - CompetitionOpenSinceYear) * 12 + (Month - CompetitionOpenSinceMonth),
             NA_real_), 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    StoreTypeLabel = toupper(StoreType),
    StoreType  = as.integer(factor(StoreType,  levels = c("a","b","c","d"))),
    Assortment = as.integer(factor(Assortment, levels = c("a","b","c")))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    CompetitionDistance   = replace_na(CompetitionDistance,
                                       median(CompetitionDistance, na.rm = TRUE)),
    CompetitionOpenMonths = replace_na(CompetitionOpenMonths, 0)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date, Store)

FEAT_S1 <- c("Store","DayOfWeek","Promo","StateHoliday","SchoolHoliday",
             "StoreType","Assortment","CompetitionDistance","Promo2",
             "Year","Month","Week","DayOfMonth","Quarter","IsWeekend",
             "CompetitionOpenMonths")
LAG_COLS  <- c("lag1","lag7","lag14","lag28")
ROLL_COLS <- c("roll7_mean","roll28_mean")
FEAT_S3   <- c(FEAT_S1, LAG_COLS, ROLL_COLS)

# Primary split: final 42 days are the test period
all_dates  <- sort(unique(df$Date))
cutoff     <- all_dates[length(all_dates) - TEST_DAYS]
train_df   <- df %>% filter(Date <= cutoff)
test_df    <- df %>% filter(Date >  cutoff)
test_dates <- sort(unique(test_df$Date))
cat("Train rows:", nrow(train_df), "| Test rows:", nrow(test_df), "\n")
```

# 2  Shared helpers

Compact fitting helpers. Early stopping uses the last 42 training days as a
temporal validation slice (cheaper than k-fold; rounded selection is then
refit on the full training data). Metric helpers mirror the comprehensive file.

```{r helpers}
rmse <- function(a, p) sqrt(mean((a - p)^2))

# --- Store-DOW baseline: mean training sales per (Store, DayOfWeek) --------
predict_store_dow <- function(train, test) {
  lookup_dow   <- train %>% group_by(Store, DayOfWeek) %>%
    summarise(p = mean(Sales), .groups = "drop")
  lookup_store <- train %>% group_by(Store) %>%
    summarise(p_store = mean(Sales), .groups = "drop")
  test %>%
    left_join(lookup_dow,   by = c("Store","DayOfWeek")) %>%
    left_join(lookup_store, by = "Store") %>%
    mutate(p = coalesce(p, p_store)) %>% pull(p)
}

# --- Temporal validation split (last 42 train days) for early stopping -----
make_es_slice <- function(train, feats) {
  tr_dates <- sort(unique(train$Date))
  val_cut  <- tr_dates[length(tr_dates) - TEST_DAYS]
  inner    <- train %>% filter(Date <= val_cut)
  val      <- train %>% filter(Date >  val_cut)
  list(X_in = as.matrix(inner[, feats]), y_in = inner$Sales,
       X_va = as.matrix(val[,   feats]), y_va = val$Sales)
}

# --- LightGBM: pick rounds on validation slice, refit on full train --------
fit_lgbm <- function(train, feats, num_leaves = 63, lr = 0.05,
                     max_rounds = 1000, seed = 42) {
  s <- make_es_slice(train, feats)
  params <- list(objective = "regression", metric = "rmse",
                 num_leaves = num_leaves, learning_rate = lr,
                 bagging_fraction = 0.8, bagging_freq = 1,
                 feature_fraction = 0.8, num_threads = N_THREADS,
                 seed = seed, bagging_seed = seed,
                 feature_fraction_seed = seed, verbosity = -1)
  es <- lightgbm::lgb.train(params, lightgbm::lgb.Dataset(s$X_in, label = s$y_in),
                            nrounds = max_rounds,
                            valids = list(val = lightgbm::lgb.Dataset(s$X_va, label = s$y_va)),
                            early_stopping_rounds = 40, verbose = -1)
  lightgbm::lgb.train(params,
                      lightgbm::lgb.Dataset(as.matrix(train[, feats]), label = train$Sales),
                      nrounds = es$best_iter, verbose = -1)
}

# --- XGBoost: same scheme ---------------------------------------------------
fit_xgb <- function(train, feats, max_depth = 6, eta = 0.1,
                    max_rounds = 300, seed = 42) {
  s <- make_es_slice(train, feats)
  params <- list(objective = "reg:squarederror", eta = eta,
                 max_depth = max_depth, subsample = 0.8,
                 colsample_bytree = 0.8, nthread = N_THREADS, seed = seed)
  es <- xgboost::xgb.train(params,
                           xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(s$X_in, label = s$y_in),
                           nrounds = max_rounds,
                           watchlist = list(val = xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(s$X_va, label = s$y_va)),
                           early_stopping_rounds = 20, verbose = 0)
  xgboost::xgb.train(params,
                     xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(as.matrix(train[, feats]), label = train$Sales),
                     nrounds = es$best_iteration, verbose = 0)
}

predict_model <- function(model, newdata, feats) {
  X <- as.matrix(newdata[, feats])
  if (inherits(model, "lgb.Booster")) predict(model, X)
  else predict(model, xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(X))
}

# --- Lag features on the open-day sequence (strictly prior days) -----------
add_lag_features <- function(store_df) {
  store_df <- store_df %>% arrange(Date)
  for (k in c(1, 7, 14, 28)) store_df[[paste0("lag", k)]] <- lag(store_df$Sales, k)
  store_df$roll7_mean  <- lag(rollmeanr(store_df$Sales, 7,  fill = NA), 1)
  store_df$roll28_mean <- lag(rollmeanr(store_df$Sales, 28, fill = NA), 1)
  store_df
}
```

# 3  Main-holdout predictions (reused by E2 and E4)

One fit per model on the no-lag feature set; row-level predictions are kept.

```{r main-holdout-preds}
lgbm_s1 <- fit_lgbm(train_df, FEAT_S1)
xgb_s1  <- fit_xgb(train_df,  FEAT_S1)

holdout <- test_df %>%
  mutate(
    pred_dow  = predict_store_dow(train_df, test_df),
    pred_lgbm = predict_model(lgbm_s1, test_df, FEAT_S1),
    pred_xgb  = predict_model(xgb_s1,  test_df, FEAT_S1)
  )

tibble(Model = c("Store-DOW","XGBoost","LightGBM"),
       RMSE  = c(rmse(holdout$Sales, holdout$pred_dow),
                 rmse(holdout$Sales, holdout$pred_xgb),
                 rmse(holdout$Sales, holdout$pred_lgbm)))
```

# 4  E1 — Fixed-origin recursive 42-day forecast (Stage 3b)

Stage 3 in the main file uses **rolling one-day-ahead** updates: realised
test-day sales feed later lag features. Here lag features during the holdout
are filled with the model's **own predictions**, so nothing after the forecast
origin is observed. The comparison then has three clean points:

1. Stage 1 (no lags, fixed origin) — information baseline,
2. Stage 3b (lags, fixed origin, recursive) — adds lag *information* only,
3. Stage 3 (lags, rolling) — additionally adds daily *updating*.

```{r e1-recursive, eval=RUN_E1_RECURSIVE}
# Train exactly as in Stage 3: actual lags, drop warm-up NA rows
train_lagged <- train_df %>% group_by(Store) %>% group_modify(~ add_lag_features(.x)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% drop_na(all_of(c(LAG_COLS, ROLL_COLS)))

lgbm_s3 <- fit_lgbm(train_lagged, FEAT_S3)
xgb_s3  <- fit_xgb(train_lagged,  FEAT_S3)

# Per-store open-day sales history (train actuals; predictions appended later)
history <- split(train_df$Sales, train_df$Store)  # named by Store, date-ordered

# Day-by-day recursion over the 42 test dates
recursive_forecast <- function(model) {
  hist_local <- history
  preds <- numeric(nrow(test_df))
  row_index <- split(seq_len(nrow(test_df)), test_df$Date)  # rows per test date

  for (d in as.character(test_dates)) {
    idx  <- row_index[[d]]
    day  <- test_df[idx, ]
    sid  <- as.character(day$Store)
    # Lag features from each store's history tail (open-day sequence)
    lagf <- t(vapply(sid, function(s) {
      h <- hist_local[[s]]; n <- length(h)
      c(h[n], h[max(1, n - 6)], h[max(1, n - 13)], h[max(1, n - 27)],
        mean(h[max(1, n - 6):n]), mean(h[max(1, n - 27):n]))
    }, numeric(6)))
    colnames(lagf) <- c(LAG_COLS, ROLL_COLS)
    X <- cbind(as.matrix(day[, FEAT_S1]), lagf)
    p <- if (inherits(model, "lgb.Booster")) predict(model, X)
         else predict(model, xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(X))
    preds[idx] <- p
    # Append PREDICTIONS (not actuals) -> fixed-origin recursion
    for (j in seq_along(sid)) {
      hist_local[[sid[j]]] <- c(hist_local[[sid[j]]], p[j])
    }
  }
  preds
}

pred_lgbm_rec <- recursive_forecast(lgbm_s3)
pred_xgb_rec  <- recursive_forecast(xgb_s3)

e1_results <- tibble(
  Model  = c("LightGBM", "XGBoost"),
  `Stage 1 (no lags, fixed origin)` = c(rmse(holdout$Sales, holdout$pred_lgbm),
                                        rmse(holdout$Sales, holdout$pred_xgb)),
  `Stage 3b (lags, fixed origin, recursive)` = c(rmse(test_df$Sales, pred_lgbm_rec),
                                                 rmse(test_df$Sales, pred_xgb_rec))
)
e1_results
write_csv(e1_results, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "tab_e1_fixed_origin_recursive.csv"))
# Interpretation: (Stage1 - Stage3b) = value of lag information at a 42-day
# horizon; (Stage3b - Stage3 rolling RMSE from the main file) = value of
# updating forecasts daily as sales are observed.
```

# 5  E2 — Diebold–Mariano tests

Forecast errors are panel-shaped (1115 stores x 42 days), while `dm.test`
expects two univariate loss series. Errors are therefore aggregated to **one
squared-error mean per test day** (42 values per model), which preserves the
temporal ordering the test requires. Squared-error loss matches the RMSE
ranking criterion.

```{r e2-dm, eval=RUN_E2_DM_TESTS}
daily_sq_loss <- function(pred) {
  tibble(Date = test_df$Date, sq = (test_df$Sales - pred)^2) %>%
    group_by(Date) %>% summarise(loss = mean(sq), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(Date) %>% pull(loss)
}

loss_lgbm <- daily_sq_loss(holdout$pred_lgbm)
loss_xgb  <- daily_sq_loss(holdout$pred_xgb)
loss_dow  <- daily_sq_loss(holdout$pred_dow)

dm_pair <- function(l1, l2, label) {
  # dm.test expects error series; with power = 2 it compares |e|^2.
  # Passing sqrt(daily mean squared loss) therefore tests exactly the
  # differential of the daily squared-loss series d_t = l1_t - l2_t.
  dm <- forecast::dm.test(sqrt(l1), sqrt(l2),
                          alternative = "two.sided", h = 1, power = 2)
  tibble(Comparison = label, DM_stat = unname(dm$statistic), p_value = dm$p.value)
}

e2_results <- bind_rows(
  dm_pair(loss_lgbm, loss_xgb, "LightGBM vs XGBoost"),
  dm_pair(loss_lgbm, loss_dow, "LightGBM vs Store-DOW"),
  dm_pair(loss_xgb,  loss_dow, "XGBoost vs Store-DOW")
)
e2_results
write_csv(e2_results, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "tab_e2_dm_tests.csv"))
```

# 6  E3 — Replication uncertainty for the number-of-stores experiment

Re-runs the N-stores conditions and reports mean **and standard deviation**
across the five seeds, so the Stage 2 table can carry uncertainty bands.

```{r e3-subset-sd, eval=RUN_E3_SUBSET_SD}
run_n_stores_once <- function(n_stores, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  stores  <- sample(unique(df$Store), n_stores)
  sub     <- df %>% filter(Store %in% stores)
  tr <- sub %>% filter(Date <= cutoff); te <- sub %>% filter(Date > cutoff)
  naive <- tr %>% group_by(Store) %>% summarise(p = mean(Sales), .groups="drop")
  p_naive <- te %>% left_join(naive, by = "Store") %>% pull(p)
  r_naive <- rmse(te$Sales, p_naive)
  gain <- function(p) 100 * (r_naive - rmse(te$Sales, p)) / r_naive
  tibble(N = n_stores, seed = seed,
         gain_xgb  = gain(predict_model(fit_xgb(tr,  FEAT_S1, seed = seed), te, FEAT_S1)),
         gain_lgbm = gain(predict_model(fit_lgbm(tr, FEAT_S1, seed = seed), te, FEAT_S1)))
}

e3_raw <- map_dfr(c(50, 200, 500),
                  function(n) map_dfr(SEEDS, function(s) run_n_stores_once(n, s)))

e3_results <- e3_raw %>% group_by(N) %>%
  summarise(across(starts_with("gain"), list(mean = mean, sd = sd)), .groups = "drop")
e3_results
write_csv(e3_results, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "tab_e3_nstores_sd.csv"))
```

# 7  E4 — Framework validation: per-store gain vs. predictable variation

The framework predicts `MSE_naive - MSE_tree ≈ Var(delta) * rho^2`: stores
with more predictable within-store variation should show larger ensemble
gains. Proxy for `Var(delta)`: the share of each store's within-store training
variance explained by DayOfWeek x Promo cell means.

```{r e4-framework, eval=RUN_E4_FRAMEWORK}
# Var(delta) proxy per store, from TRAINING data only
var_delta <- train_df %>%
  group_by(Store) %>%
  mutate(cell_mean = ave(Sales, DayOfWeek, Promo)) %>%
  summarise(
    var_total     = var(Sales),
    var_explained = var(cell_mean),                 # predictable component
    share_pred    = var_explained / var_total,
    mean_sales    = mean(Sales), .groups = "drop")

# Per-store RMSE gain of LightGBM over Store-DOW on the holdout
store_gain <- holdout %>% group_by(Store) %>%
  summarise(rmse_dow  = rmse(Sales, pred_dow),
            rmse_lgbm = rmse(Sales, pred_lgbm), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(gain_pct = 100 * (rmse_dow - rmse_lgbm) / rmse_dow)

e4 <- inner_join(var_delta, store_gain, by = "Store")
cor_test <- cor.test(e4$var_explained, e4$rmse_dow^2 - e4$rmse_lgbm^2)
cat("Correlation Var(delta)-proxy vs MSE gain:",
    round(cor_test$estimate, 3), " p =", format.pval(cor_test$p.value), "\n")

p_framework <- ggplot(e4, aes(var_explained / 1e6, (rmse_dow^2 - rmse_lgbm^2) / 1e6)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Predictable within-store variance (millions, train)",
       y = "MSE reduction vs Store-DOW (millions, test)",
       title = "Framework check: predictable variation vs realised ensemble gain") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
p_framework
ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "fig_framework_test.pdf"), p_framework,
       width = 7, height = 4.2)
write_csv(e4, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "tab_e4_store_level_framework.csv"))
```

# 8  E5 — Hyperparameter sensitivity grid

Is "LightGBM beats XGBoost" robust to capacity choices, or an artefact of
63 leaves vs. depth 6? No-lag features, primary holdout.

```{r e5-grid, eval=RUN_E5_GRID}
e5_results <- bind_rows(
  map_dfr(c(6, 8, 10), function(d) {
    m <- fit_xgb(train_df, FEAT_S1, max_depth = d)
    tibble(Model = "XGBoost", Setting = paste0("max_depth = ", d),
           RMSE = rmse(test_df$Sales, predict_model(m, test_df, FEAT_S1)))
  }),
  map_dfr(c(31, 63, 127), function(nl) {
    m <- fit_lgbm(train_df, FEAT_S1, num_leaves = nl)
    tibble(Model = "LightGBM", Setting = paste0("num_leaves = ", nl),
           RMSE = rmse(test_df$Sales, predict_model(m, test_df, FEAT_S1)))
  })
)
e5_results %>% arrange(RMSE)
write_csv(e5_results, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "tab_e5_hyperparameter_grid.csv"))
```

# 9  E6 — Scale experiment with fixed composition (Type A only)

Prediction 1 (more stores -> larger gain) was rejected, but the mixed subsets
confound scale with composition. Sampling only Type A stores holds
composition fixed.

```{r e6-typea, eval=RUN_E6_TYPEA_SCALE}
stores_a <- df %>% filter(StoreTypeLabel == "A") %>% distinct(Store) %>% pull(Store)

run_typea_once <- function(n_stores, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  sub <- df %>% filter(Store %in% sample(stores_a, n_stores))
  tr <- sub %>% filter(Date <= cutoff); te <- sub %>% filter(Date > cutoff)
  naive <- tr %>% group_by(Store) %>% summarise(p = mean(Sales), .groups="drop")
  r_naive <- rmse(te$Sales, te %>% left_join(naive, by="Store") %>% pull(p))
  gain <- function(p) 100 * (r_naive - rmse(te$Sales, p)) / r_naive
  tibble(N = n_stores, seed = seed,
         gain_xgb  = gain(predict_model(fit_xgb(tr,  FEAT_S1, seed = seed), te, FEAT_S1)),
         gain_lgbm = gain(predict_model(fit_lgbm(tr, FEAT_S1, seed = seed), te, FEAT_S1)))
}

e6_results <- map_dfr(c(50, 200, 500), function(n)
    map_dfr(SEEDS, function(s) run_typea_once(n, s))) %>%
  group_by(N) %>%
  summarise(across(starts_with("gain"), list(mean = mean, sd = sd)), .groups = "drop")
e6_results
write_csv(e6_results, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "tab_e6_typea_scale.csv"))
# Compare with E3: if the downward trend disappears here, composition (not
# scale itself) drove the rejection of Prediction 1.
```

# 10  E7 — Global vs. local LightGBM

One global model pooled across stores vs. one small LightGBM per store,
compared on the same random store sample (full 1115 local fits are
unnecessarily slow; the sample is representative and seeded).

```{r e7-global-local, eval=RUN_E7_GLOBAL_LOCAL}
set.seed(42)
sample_stores <- sample(unique(df$Store), N_LOCAL_STORES)

# Global predictions restricted to the sample (reuse Section 3 model)
glob <- holdout %>% filter(Store %in% sample_stores)

# Local: per-store LightGBM with conservative capacity (small samples)
local_one <- function(s) {
  tr <- train_df %>% filter(Store == s); te <- test_df %>% filter(Store == s)
  if (nrow(te) == 0) return(NULL)
  feats <- setdiff(FEAT_S1, c("Store","StoreType","Assortment",
                              "CompetitionDistance","Promo2"))  # store-constant cols dropped
  m <- lightgbm::lgb.train(
    params = list(objective = "regression", metric = "rmse", num_leaves = 15,
                  learning_rate = 0.05, min_data_in_leaf = 20,
                  num_threads = 1, seed = 42, verbosity = -1),
    data = lightgbm::lgb.Dataset(as.matrix(tr[, feats]), label = tr$Sales),
    nrounds = 300, verbose = -1)
  tibble(Store = s, Sales = te$Sales,
         pred_local = predict(m, as.matrix(te[, feats])))
}
local_preds <- map_dfr(sample_stores, local_one)

e7_results <- tibble(
  Model = c("Global LightGBM", "Local LightGBM (per store)"),
  RMSE  = c(rmse(glob$Sales, glob$pred_lgbm),
            rmse(local_preds$Sales, local_preds$pred_local)),
  Stores = N_LOCAL_STORES
)
e7_results
write_csv(e7_results, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "tab_e7_global_vs_local.csv"))
```

# 11  E8 — Descriptive statistics and EDA exports

Tables and figures for the new Data section of the thesis.

```{r e8-descriptives}
# --- Store-type table: counts, Sunday opening, sales level -----------------
sunday_share <- train_raw %>%
  left_join(store_raw %>% select(Store, StoreType), by = "Store") %>%
  filter(DayOfWeek == 7) %>%
  group_by(StoreType) %>%
  summarise(sunday_open_share = mean(Open), .groups = "drop")

e8_storetypes <- df %>%
  group_by(StoreTypeLabel) %>%
  summarise(N_stores = n_distinct(Store),
            mean_sales = mean(Sales),
            dow_var_share = {            # predictable weekly share (pooled proxy)
              cm <- ave(Sales, Store, DayOfWeek); var(cm) / var(Sales)
            }, .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(sunday_share %>% mutate(StoreTypeLabel = toupper(StoreType)) %>%
              select(-StoreType), by = "StoreTypeLabel")
e8_storetypes
write_csv(e8_storetypes, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "tab_e8_store_types.csv"))

# --- Overall descriptive statistics ----------------------------------------
e8_summary <- tibble(
  Statistic = c("Stores", "Open-day observations", "Date range",
                "Mean daily sales", "Median daily sales", "SD daily sales",
                "Promo-day share", "School-holiday share"),
  Value = c(n_distinct(df$Store), nrow(df),
            paste(min(df$Date), "to", max(df$Date)),
            round(mean(df$Sales)), round(median(df$Sales)), round(sd(df$Sales)),
            round(mean(df$Promo), 3), round(mean(df$SchoolHoliday), 3)))
e8_summary
write_csv(e8_summary, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "tab_e8_descriptives.csv"))

# --- Day-of-week profile figure ---------------------------------------------
p_dow <- df %>% group_by(DayOfWeek) %>% summarise(m = mean(Sales)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(factor(DayOfWeek), m)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(x = "Day of week (1 = Monday)", y = "Mean open-day sales (EUR)",
       title = "Average sales by day of week") + theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "fig_eda_dow_profile.pdf"), p_dow, width = 6, height = 3.5)

# --- Example store series (one per store type) ------------------------------
set.seed(42)
example_stores <- df %>% group_by(StoreTypeLabel) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 1) %>% pull(Store)
p_series <- df %>% filter(Store %in% example_stores, Year == 2014) %>%
  ggplot(aes(Date, Sales)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.25, colour = "grey30") +
  facet_wrap(~ paste0("Store ", Store, " (Type ", StoreTypeLabel, ")"),
             scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(title = "Example daily sales series, 2014") + theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "fig_eda_example_series.pdf"), p_series,
       width = 7, height = 7)
p_dow; p_series
```
